questions.text: Where do diet and allergies appear, and how are they saved?
options: On the Profile screen, as a separate section below the six profile fields, with its own Save button (as in mock.md)
On the Profile screen, saved together with the six profile fields by the one Save button
On a separate 'Diet & allergies' screen with its own Save button
questions.reason: REQ-407 says the values are 'saved with the profile', and its mock shows its own Save button, while the REQ-406 Profile page saves its six required fields together. The answer decides the screen layout and whether diet and allergies use the profile endpoint or their own.
questions.answer: On the Profile screen, as a separate section below the six profile fields, with its own Save button (as in mock.md)

questions.text: Is the diet preference (vegetarian or non-vegetarian) optional?
options: Optional: it can be left unset, and the user can clear it again
Optional until set: once chosen it can be changed between the two but not cleared
Required: the section cannot be saved without choosing one
questions.reason: REQ-407 only says the user 'can choose'. REQ-406 says diet does not count for a complete profile, and profiles.diet_type allows empty. Whether it can be left empty or cleared changes validation and the form.
questions.answer: Optional: it can be left unset, and the user can clear it again

questions.text: How should allergy names be stored and matched?
options: Trim spaces at both ends, keep the user's spelling, and refuse a duplicate ignoring letter case ('Peanuts' = 'peanuts')
Trim spaces and store in lower case, refusing duplicates
Keep exactly as typed; only identical names count as duplicates
questions.reason: The DB design stores one free-text row per allergy with UNIQUE (user_id, name), but does not say whether 'Peanuts' and ' peanuts' are the same allergy. Meal plans (REQ-413) will match on these names.
questions.answer: Trim spaces at both ends, keep the user's spelling, and refuse a duplicate ignoring letter case ('Peanuts' = 'peanuts')

options: Name 1 to 50 characters; at most 20 allergies per user
Name 1 to 100 characters; no limit on the number
No limits beyond a non-empty name
questions.reason: Neither REQ-407 nor the DB design sets a maximum name length or number of allergies; the API needs a rule to validate against.
questions.answer: Name 1 to 50 characters; at most 20 allergies per user
